answer: Here is one mechanism that works: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because kernel only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, ember is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any atlas approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
